newsitem.title: FRANCE: France deeply concerned about tension with Iraq.
newsitem.headline: France deeply concerned about tension with Iraq.

text.p: France said on Thursday it was deeply concerned at mounting tension after Iraq fired a missile at U.S. warplanes patrolling over northern Iraq and called for consultation among the Western allies before any response.

"We are in contact with the United States and we believe it is necessary for the partners in operation Provide Comfort to continue to consult on their evaluation of the situation and on their intentions," foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said in a statement.
U.S. stealth fighter-bombers were on their way to the Gulf for what seemed almost certain retaliation against Iraqi President Saddam Hussein for Wednesday's missile attack.

The French statement made no mention of U.S. threats of "disproportionate" retaliation against Iraq. But France voiced disapproval last week after President Bill Clinton launched cruise missile strikes in reaction to Baghdad sending troops into Kurdish areas of northern Iraq.

"France, which participates alongside the United States, Britain and Turkey in Provide Comfort air patrols, is deeply concerned by the rise in tension after an Iraqi missile was fired on Wednesday afternoon at an American plane during a surveillance mission north of the 36th parallel," Rummelhardt said.

Paris was part of the Gulf War coalition that drove Iraqi invasion forces out of Kuwait in 1991 and has since helped patrol two no-fly zones in northern and southern Iraq designed to protect civilian Kurdish and Shi'ite minorities.
However, it refused to join the United States and Britain in patrolling an enlarged exclusion zone after Clinton extended it northwards to the 34th parallel.

Asked whether the situation had changed since France dissociated itself from last week's U.S. action, Rummelhardt told a briefing: "It is not we who have changed the situation. It is the firing of the Iraqi missile."
Since last week's U.S. raids, a Kurdish faction backed by Baghdad has extended its hold over northern Iraq although Iraqi troops are reported to have withdrawn from the area.
France has said the international community cannot intervene in fighting between rival Kurdish guerrilla movements.

Defence officials said French planes were participating normally in patrols over southern Iraq despite the tension and there had been no change since the U.S. decision to send F-117 stealth aircraft to Kuwait for a possible strike.

Jean-Claude Mallet, the ministry's director of strategic affairs, said French air forces in the Gulf had been instructed to seek clearance from Paris if asked to come to the assistance of the stealth planes.
"The question would be sent back to the (French) government for study," he told reporters.
